scope: Independent adversarial data audit (DA8) of five current-holding dossiers not previously checked by this auditor: AMP, ADP, CRH, PGR, DOV. 33 load-bearing facts checked (7/7/7/6/6 by ticker), selected for the claims most likely to break a thesis or a kill criterion if wrong: headline quarterly figures, guidance track records, leverage/capital ratios, deal terms/dates, litigation status, and capital-return figures. Method: primary sources only -- SEC EDGAR 8-K Ex-99.1 earnings-release exhibits, 10-Q/10-K text and notes, and data.sec.gov XBRL companyfacts/companyconcept pulls -- fetched directly from www.sec.gov and data.sec.gov and cited by accession/URL below. Each dossier was read to its end (no appended Correction sections were found on any of the five). Each ticker's one-line thesis and first kill criterion were checked for consistency with the underlying filings; results noted in the relevant fact or in the summary below (see da8_factcheck.md section 4 for the explicit per-ticker kill-criterion-1 consistency check).

facts.claim: Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS $10.39 (footnoted as "derived as the 10-K annual figure minus the sum of the three preceding 10-Qs, standard convention")
facts.dossier_location: AMP.md §4 results table, Q4 2025 row and footnote 1
facts.source: AMP 8-K Ex-99.1, Q4/FY2025 earnings release, accession embedded in URL 000082002726000004, filed 2026-01-29
facts.source_value: "GAAP net income per diluted share was $10.47 compared to $10.58 a year ago" (directly reported Q4 2025 figure, not derived)
facts.note: Actual, directly-reported Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS is $10.47, not the $10.39 the dossier derives by subtracting Q1-Q3 2025 EPS from the FY2025 total. This subtraction method is unsound for diluted EPS because weighted-average share counts differ by quarter (a fully-diluted quarterly EPS is not the simple residual of the annual figure). The ~0.8% gap is immaterial to any conclusion in this dossier, but the same derivation-method risk that DA7 flagged for GM's Q1/Q4 2025/2026 cells recurs here.

facts.claim: TTM ROE ~62% (net income ~$3.9-4.0bn / stockholders' equity $6.37bn); thesis and kill criterion 1 ("TTM ROE falls below 40%") consistency
facts.source: AMP 8-K Ex-99.1, Q2 2026 earnings release, Consolidated GAAP Results and Balance Sheet
facts.source_value: Twelve-months-ended net income $3,948m; Total Equity (balance sheet, 30-Jun-2026) $6,366m → 3,948/6,366 = 62.0%
facts.note: The dossier's raw TTM-NI/period-end-equity calculation (62.0%) matches exactly and is internally consistent with kill criterion 1's 40% threshold. Note for context: this differs methodologically from AMP's own primary disclosed metric, "Return on Equity, ex. AOCI" (53.0% GAAP / 55.0% Adjusted Operating, calculated on a 5-point-average-equity-excluding-AOCI basis) -- both are legitimate, differently-defined ROE figures, and the dossier is transparent that its 62% figure is its own/V1's calculation, not the company's own headline ROE metric.

facts.claim: "$48M settlement (Aug-2026, preliminary approval pending) in a 401(k)/TotalSource retirement-plan fee ERISA class action ... A separate ERISA suit re: the ADP TotalSource Retirement Savings Plan (filed 2020, New Jersey) remains open; ADP states it cannot estimate a reasonably possible loss"
facts.source: ADP FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-08-05), Note 13 Commitments and Contingencies
facts.source_value: "In May 2020, a putative class action complaint was filed against ADP, TotalSource and related defendants in the U.S. District Court, District of New Jersey. The complaint asserts violations of [ERISA] in connection with the ADP TotalSource Retirement Savings Plan's fiduciary administrative and investment decision-making. The Company reached a settlement of all outstanding claims for $48 million, subject to the court's approval." No other ERISA/TotalSource retirement-plan matter appears in the note.
facts.note: The 10-K describes only ONE matter -- the May-2020, New Jersey, TotalSource Retirement Savings Plan ERISA suit -- and it is the SAME suit that reached the $48M settlement (subject to court approval). The dossier's litigation paragraph describes this as two separate items: a settled $48M matter, plus "a separate" still-open ERISA suit with an identical description (filed 2020, New Jersey, TotalSource Retirement Savings Plan). No such second, open matter exists in the current 10-K; this appears to be stale language (describing the pre-settlement status of the same case) mistakenly presented as a distinct, currently-open second case in the red-flag scan.

facts.claim: Net debt at 30-Jun-2026 ≈$14.9bn (own calculation: total debt ≈$17.93bn less cash $3.025bn), used for the ≈1.8x net debt/EBITDA leverage figure
facts.source: CRH 8-K Ex-99.1, Q2 2026 results announcement, Balance Sheet and Liquidity section
facts.source_value: "Total short and long-term debt was $17.9 billion at June 30, 2026 ... Net Debt* at June 30, 2026, was $15.4 billion, compared to $14.2 billion at December 31, 2025 ... $3.1 billion of cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash on hand"
facts.note: CRH itself discloses a non-GAAP "Net Debt*" of $15.4bn at 30-Jun-2026 (up from $14.2bn at FY2025-end), not the $14.9bn the dossier derives by subtracting cash from total debt -- CRH's own Net Debt definition evidently nets against a narrower cash base or includes items (e.g., lease liabilities) the dossier's simple subtraction omits. Using the company's own $15.4bn figure, net debt/EBITDA is ≈1.86x (vs the dossier's stated ≈1.8x) -- the conclusion (moderate, investment-grade-consistent leverage, well under the 3.0x kill-criterion threshold) is unaffected, but the specific $14.9bn net-debt figure does not match CRH's own reported metric.
